notes: Assertions that depend on a GitHub remote are conditional here: this repo has no .git directory, and check-readme.ts fails a README that asserts one anyway.

evals.prompt: Improve the README for this project
evals.expected_output: A polished README.md with all supportable sections filled in from actual project data
assertions: Has a centered hero section with the project name and a short tagline
Includes shields.io badges with style=for-the-badge only for status indicators the scan actually found; includes no badges at all if the scan found none
Has a What is this section that describes the project in 2-3 sentences
Has a Quick Start section with real install and run commands based on the detected package manager, or replaces it with a document map when the project has no runnable code
Includes a project structure tree generated from the actual file system, with folders shown before files
Has a documentation table linking to real files in the repo
Includes contributor avatars from contrib.rocks only when the scan reports a GitHub owner and repo
Only includes social badges for links that actually exist in the project
Includes a star history chart only when the scan reports a GitHub owner and repo
Does not contain placeholder text like {{PROJECT_NAME}} or TODO

evals.prompt: My repo needs a better README, can you make it look professional?
evals.expected_output: A professional README.md that transforms a basic or empty README into a polished one
assertions: Has a centered hero section with the project name and a short tagline
Includes shields.io badges with style=for-the-badge for every status indicator the scan supports
Has a What is this section that accurately describes what the project does
Has a Quick Start section with real commands, not generic placeholders
Includes a project structure tree with folders shown before files
Does not fabricate social media links that don't exist in the project
Does not include badges for CI workflows that don't exist
Writing tone is concise and direct, not marketing fluff

evals.prompt: Generate a README for this project. It's just a small script, nothing fancy.
evals.expected_output: A concise README that is proportional to the project size — not bloated with unnecessary sections
assertions: Has a project title and description
Has a Quick Start or Usage section showing how to run the script
Does not include empty or stub sections
Does not fabricate metadata that doesn't exist in the project
README length is proportional to the project complexity — not excessively long for a simple project
Does not contain placeholder text like {{PROJECT_NAME}} or TODO

evals.prompt: I want to add some nice badges to my README, the shields.io kind. Can you help?
evals.expected_output: README with properly formatted shields.io badges based on actual project metadata
assertions: All badges use style=for-the-badge
Badge URLs point to shields.io
No badges reference nonexistent CI workflows or packages
Status badges are grouped together at the top
Badge links point to the correct GitHub pages (stargazers, releases, actions, etc.)
Explains that no badges can be added when the project has no GitHub remote, rather than adding badges that would render broken

evals.prompt: Write a README for this project
evals.context: Run against a directory with no .git directory, such as this repo.
evals.expected_output: A README built entirely from local files, with every GitHub-dependent element omitted
assertions: scan-project.ts completes successfully and reports is_git_repo false without a git error
Contains no img.shields.io/github/ badge URLs
Contains no contrib.rocks contributor avatar block
Contains no star-history.com chart
Does not invent a clone URL, owner, or repository name
check-readme.ts run with --scan reports zero failures

evals.context: prod-agent has no src/, no package.json, and 11 specification documents in .research/.
evals.expected_output: A README that describes a specification-phase project honestly
assertions: States within the first paragraph that the project has no implementation yet
Does not present install or run commands for software that does not exist
Maps the .research/ documents and identifies which are superseded
Agrees with CLAUDE.md rather than contradicting it
Uses no marketing vocabulary banned by .claude/rules/design-standards.md
Names bun as the package manager if any command appears at all
